newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria amends central bank law for currency board.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria amends central bank law for currency board.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Thursday completed amendments to the central bank law that adjusts its operation to the requirements of an IMF-prescribed currency board system designed to stabilise the economy.
"Voting on the amendments to the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) law has been completed and the law hereby is passed," parliament's speaker Yordan Sokolov told parliament.

The law will come into force after being published in the State Gazette on Friday or Monday, except for articles concerning the lev/mark fixed rate peg of 1,000, which are due to be enforced on July 1, when the currency board is launched. The mark is set as anchor currency.

The law transforms the BNB into three departments. The Issue Department implements the currency board overseeing that levs in circulation are fully matched by foreign exchange reserves, estimated to be around $1 billion at time of introduction.
Under the law BNB capital is set at 20 billion levs.
A Banking Department manages the lender of last resort role and reserve requirements for commercial banks with the aim of ensuring the functioning of financial markets.

The currency board system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks, but the law allows the banking department to lend up to a three-month lev credit to a solvent bank if facing systemic risk.
The Banking Department can do so by ordering a transfer of funds from its deposit at the issue department to the account of the bank.
The third department, the Bank Supervision Department, enforces prudential regulations and banking laws with the objective of ensuring soundness of the banking system.

The seven-member BNB board will consist of a governor, three deputy governors, each responsible for one of the three departments to be appointed by parliament and three board members to be proposed by the president. Only Bulgarian citizens can be appointed in the BNB board, due to be elected after the law comes in effect next week.
Former interim Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski is nominated by the cabinet as the new BNB governor, to succeed Lyubomir Flilipov.

The issue department, is expected to publish a weekly balance sheet and will consist of the current Currency Issue Department, Forex operations and part of the Budget Division of the State Credits Department.

It has no independent policy other than following its operating rules. The issue department can buy or sell its lev liabilities at a fixed exchange rate for the peg currency on demand. Any foreign currency deposit liabilities are due to be matched by high-quality foreign currency assets of the same denomination, so the department takes no foreign exchange risk.
The issue department never provides credit to any account holder. The banking department lends only against a collateral in gold or hard currency.
Parliament has yet to pass this year's budget and a banking law to complete preparations for launching the currency board, which aims to restore confidence in the weak lev and banking system.
